Patrick David Gillespie

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 33, Dallas County, Texas · Open seat

Customs entry writer (UPS) – unconfirmed secondary source

Patrick David Gillespie is the Republican nominee for Texas' 33rd Congressional District. He came first in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 35.5% of the vote, then beat John Sims in the May 26, 2026 runoff. He faces Democrat Colin Allred on November 3, 2026, after running for this seat in 2022 and 2024 and losing the 2024 general election to Marc Veasey.

Where Gillespie stands

Cost of living / economy
Says wages are an equal exchange for labor, not a capital gain, and should not be subject to income tax. Says he would push to rewrite tax law to reflect that.
Cost of living / economy
Supports a free enterprise system without government interference or subsidies. Opposes student loan forgiveness.
Health care / prescription drugs
Says private insurance was affordable before the Affordable Care Act. Supports restoring Medicare funding that he says Congress cut by $500 billion.
Immigration
Supports more physical security at the southern border and favors immigrants being vetted. Says weak leadership is encouraging illegal crossings and causing a humanitarian crisis.
Immigration
Wants to reduce immigration. Opposes selling land to foreign persons, especially near military bases.
Education
Supports school choice, including vouchers and charter schools. Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning control to states.
Abortion
Opposes taxpayer funding for abortion providers. Supports banning abortion drugs and says states, not the federal government, should decide abortion policy.
Foreign policy
Says the Chinese Communist Party poses serious military, cybersecurity, and economic threats. Supports a strong relationship with Israel and 'peace through strength'.
